scenes.heading: context Package
scenes.narration: Let's understand the context package, Go's standard way to say 'stop what you're doing' across goroutines and API boundaries.

scenes.heading: What a Context carries
items: A Done() channel that closes on cancel or timeout
An Err() explaining why it stopped
scenes.narration: A Context bundles three things. First, a Done channel that closes when the operation should stop. Second, an Err method that reports why it stopped — either Canceled or DeadlineExceeded. And third, an optional Value lookup for request-scoped data like a trace ID. A context is immutable; you derive new ones from a parent rather than mutating it.

scenes.heading: How cancellation propagates
steps: Derive a context with WithTimeout and defer cancel
Fan out, passing ctx to each worker
Every listener unblocks and returns ctx.Err()
scenes.narration: Contexts form a tree. A handler derives a child with WithTimeout and defers its cancel function, then fans out to workers, passing the context to each. When the timeout fires — or a parent is cancelled — the Done channel closes as a broadcast, every worker listening on it unblocks at once, and they return promptly with ctx.Err. Cancelling a parent cancels all of its descendants.

scenes.heading: Derive, defer cancel, honor Done
scenes.narration: Here fetch derives a one-second timeout from its parent and immediately defers cancel, which releases the context's timer even on an early return. It passes the context down to worker, which cooperatively selects on ctx.Done. Because the timeout is one second but the work takes two, Done fires first and worker returns ctx.Err. Cancellation is cooperative — the worker has to check Done for it to matter.

scenes.text: Cancellation only closes Done() — nothing is killed for you. And always call cancel, or you leak a timer.
scenes.narration: Two pitfalls to remember. Cancelling a context does not kill any goroutines; it only closes the Done channel, so your code must actually check it and return. And you must always call the cancel function, idiomatically with defer, or you leak the context's timer and bookkeeping.

scenes.text: Pass ctx as the first argument, never store it in a struct — one deadline flows through every layer.
scenes.narration: By convention, Context is the first parameter of any function that does I/O or could block, and you never stash it in a struct field. Passing it explicitly down the call chain is what lets a single deadline propagate cleanly through every layer of a request.
